# Reporting: Methods, wording and claims {#sec-report}

An analysis is only as useful as its description. This chapter turns the
previous ones into text you could put in a thesis or paper: a Methods
paragraph with every parameter that matters, results sentences that say
exactly what the data show, and a checklist that separates **statistically
significant** from **validated**.


::: {.cell layout-align="center"}

```{.r .cell-code}
source("R/helpers.R")
suppressPackageStartupMessages(library(dplyr))
de    <- read.csv("results/de_deseq2_TDP43_vs_scramble.csv")
cand  <- read.csv("results/cryptic_junction_candidates.csv")
gsea  <- read.csv("results/gsea_hallmark_TDP43_vs_scramble.csv")
rmats <- read.csv("results/rmats_demo_significant_JC.csv")
v <- function(p) as.character(packageVersion(p))
n_de <- sum(de$DE != "not significant")
tools <- readLines("data/demo/tool_versions.txt")
tool_v <- function(pattern) sub("^.*?([0-9]+\\.[0-9.]+).*$", "\\1", grep(pattern, tools, value = TRUE)[1])
```
:::


## Methods: what to write

Every number below is filled in from the analysis itself, so the text cannot
drift away from the code.

::: {.callout-note appearance="minimal"}
**Data.** We reanalysed RNA-seq data of motor neurons differentiated from
the human embryonic stem cell line HUES3 and transfected with siRNA against
*TARDBP* (n = 6) or a non-targeting scramble siRNA (n = 6) [@klim2019; SRA
SRP166282, GEO GSE121569]. Libraries were prepared with the Illumina TruSeq
RNA kit v2 and sequenced paired-end (2 x 76 bp) in two batches. Gene and
splice junction counts were obtained from recount3 [@wilks2021] (R package
recount3 1.16.0), in which reads were aligned to GRCh38 and
summarised with GENCODE release 26 [@frankish2019]. GENCODE v26 was used for
all annotation-based steps. Base-pair coverage sums were converted to read
counts with `compute_read_counts()`.

**Differential expression.** Genes with at least 10 counts in at least 6
samples (the size of the smallest group) were kept
(20,683 genes). Differential expression was
tested with DESeq2 1.46.0 [@love2014] using the design
`~ batch + condition`, with scramble siRNA as the reference level. Log2 fold
changes were shrunk with apeglm 1.28.0 [@zhu2019]. Genes with a
Benjamini-Hochberg adjusted p-value below 0.05 and an absolute shrunken log2
fold change above 1 were called differentially expressed. Thresholds were
set before the analysis. Results were compared with edgeR 4.4.0
quasi-likelihood F-tests [@chen2016] on the same genes and design. As a
sensitivity analysis for unrecorded batch effects, surrogate variables were
estimated with svaseq (sva 3.54.0) [@leek2014]; the number of
surrogate variables was chosen with the permutation method of `num.sv()`.

**Gene set enrichment.** Genes were ranked by the DESeq2 Wald statistic and
tested against the 50 MSigDB Hallmark gene sets [@liberzon2015] (msigdbr
7.5.1) with fgsea 1.32.2 [@korotkevich2019] (gene set
size 15 to 500, random seed 42). Gene sets with adjusted p < 0.05 are
reported.

**Splice junctions and cryptic exons.** Junctions not matching a GENCODE v26
intron exactly were considered unannotated. Junction usage was defined as
the junction's read count divided by the larger of the total counts at its
donor and at its acceptor site. A junction was a cryptic candidate if it was
unannotated, had at least 3 reads in at least 4 of 6 knockdown samples, and
either (A) had at most 2 reads in total in controls and at least 20 in the
knockdown, or (B) had mean usage below 0.05 in controls and at least 0.1
higher in the knockdown. Candidates were inspected in sashimi-style plots of
recount3 coverage and junction counts.

**Event-level splicing (demonstration).** For 3 knockdown and 3 scramble
samples of batch B2, reads of a predefined panel of 17 genes were aligned to
GRCh38 with HISAT2 NA [@kim2019], keeping properly paired,
uniquely aligned reads. Strandedness was measured with RSeQC
infer_experiment [@wang2012] and featureCounts 2.1.1
[@liao2014] and found to be unstranded. Differential splicing was tested
with rMATS-turbo 4.3.0 [@shen2014; @wang2024]
(`-t paired --readLength 76 --libType fr-unstranded --novelSS`;
b1 = knockdown, b2 = scramble, so ΔPSI = PSI(knockdown) - PSI(scramble)).
Junction-count (JC) results are reported; events were called significant at
FDR < 0.05, |ΔPSI| > 0.1 and a mean of at least 10 informative reads
(IJC + SJC) per sample. The FDR refers to the events of the 17-gene panel.
:::

A few things to notice about this text:

- It names the **replicate unit and n per group**, the **batch handling**,
  the **reference level**, and the **direction** of every difference.
- It gives the **annotation release** and genome, and says that one
  annotation was used throughout.
- It states **thresholds and when they were fixed**, and the **multiple
  testing family** (genome-wide for DE, the 17-gene panel for rMATS).
- It gives **versions** of every package that changes the numbers.

## Results: wording that matches the evidence

Compare these pairs of sentences:

| Overstated | Matches the evidence |
|---|---|
| "TDP-43 knockdown downregulates 60 genes." | "60 genes passed padj < 0.05 and \|log2FC\| > 1 (23 lower and 37 higher in the knockdown)." |
| "STMN2 protein is lost after TDP-43 knockdown." | "*STMN2* mRNA was lower in the knockdown (log2FC -1.11, padj 3.7e-49)." |
| "TDP-43 loss induces a cryptic exon in UNC13A." | "Junction reads consistent with the published *UNC13A* cryptic exon were found in knockdown samples only, but at low counts that did not meet our predefined criteria (exploratory signal)." |
| "The cryptic exon causes nonsense-mediated decay." | "The cryptic exon is not a multiple of three nucleotides and is predicted to introduce a premature termination codon." |
| "Interferon signalling is activated." | "Hallmark interferon response gene sets were shifted towards higher expression in the knockdown (GSEA, ranking by Wald statistic)." |

## Significant is not the same as validated

These words mean different things and should not be used interchangeably:

- **Statistically significant**: passed a predefined statistical threshold
  in this data set. It is a statement about the data and the test.
- **Exploratory signal**: consistent with a hypothesis (for example the
  expected direction), but did not pass the predefined threshold. Worth
  following up; not a finding.
- **Validated**: confirmed by an independent method or independent samples,
  ideally both. RNA-seq cannot validate itself.

What would validate the claims in this book?

| Claim | Evidence from RNA-seq here | Independent validation |
|---|---|---|
| *STMN2* mRNA decreases | DESeq2 and edgeR, padj < 0.05 | RT-qPCR with primers in constitutive exons, in new cultures |
| *STMN2* cryptic exon appears | Junction counts in 6/6 knockdown samples, coverage plot | RT-PCR or RT-qPCR with a primer spanning the exon 1 to exon 2a junction; second siRNA |
| STMN2 protein decreases | none | Western blot or immunostaining |
| Cryptic exon transcript is degraded by NMD | none (sequence prediction only) | Block NMD (cycloheximide or UPF1 knockdown) and measure the cryptic isoform |
| Effect is caused by TDP-43 loss, not by the siRNA sequence | one siRNA only | Second independent siRNA or rescue with siRNA-resistant TDP-43 |
| Pathway "activation" | GSEA on mRNA | Functional assay of the pathway |

## A checklist for every reported result

For each number that leaves your analysis, you should be able to state:

- [ ] data set ID and number of samples per group;
- [ ] genome and annotation release;
- [ ] the statistical test, the threshold, and when it was fixed;
- [ ] the multiple-testing family (genome-wide, gene set, gene panel);
- [ ] direction of the comparison (which group is the reference);
- [ ] software versions and analysis date;
- [ ] whether the result is significant, exploratory or validated.

::: {.callout-tip}
## Check your understanding
1. Rewrite "TDP-43 regulates 60 genes" so that it matches the evidence.
2. Why does the rMATS paragraph mention the 17-gene panel?
3. A result has padj = 0.08 and the expected direction. How do you describe
   it?
4. What is the minimum additional experiment that would let you write that
   a cryptic exon is "validated"?

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}
## Answers
1. For example: "After TDP-43 knockdown, 60 genes passed padj < 0.05 and
   |log2FC| > 1 compared with scramble siRNA (DESeq2, n = 6 per group)."
   "Regulates" implies direct, causal control, which RNA-seq after
   knockdown cannot show.
2. Because the FDR was computed over the events in those genes only. A
   reader must know the multiple-testing family to interpret the FDR.
3. As an exploratory signal: consistent in direction, not significant at
   the predefined threshold.
4. An independent measurement of the junction, typically RT-PCR or RT-qPCR
   with a junction-spanning primer, in independent samples.
:::
:::
